data.translation: Der älteste sagte: »Die schönste ist für mich«; aber ein anderer Prinz schlug vor: »Wir wollen die älteste dem ältesten und die mittlere dem mittleren und die jüngste dem jüngsten geben«. So verteilten sie sie unter sich.

summary: Restore corpus ʕam before am=miṯe
rationale: 25/65 reads fləġli ak kallatani kulle ʕam am miṯe. The quotation substitutes ʕal for ʕam, changing the preposition's final consonant. Preserve the normalized article boundary am=miṯe while restoring the corpus word.

summary: Restore ṣ in ʕaṣro (ten)
rationale: The cited verse has ʕaṣro kallat, with emphatic ṣ. The supplied dictionary also lists ʕaṣro as ten. The quotation has plain s, a consonant transcription error.

summary: Active separation with m- (PrS 13/13; 95/4) is distinct from transitive apportionment. Political spitting of a community (Lahdo interviews) is a figurative specialisation; the two interviews describe the same legal allegation, not independent historical events.

Distribution recipients occur with ʕal and l-, co-participants with ʕam. Postverbal l-NPs can be agents: PrS 77/25 names the fox and dog as joint dividers, so l- must not automatically be labelled recipient.

Detransitive Infinitiv floġ is retained in its inherited box even when it names the active skill of dividing. Part. Pass. flíġewayne expresses a divided state; Infectum Koməfloġi describes a group dividing itself.

New Infectum-wa and Preterit-wa boxes contrast habitual allocation and anterior completed division. Bare flaġən addressed to a singular animal is Imperativ, correcting the reader’s isolated inclusive-Infectum analysis at PrS 82/19.

Read-only lookup confirms plġ has a single I Preterit division example and the same MEA etymology. The p/f alternation warrants editorial cross-reference review, but no wholesale merger or replacement of spelling is proposed.
At 113/5, does fliġ lebe mean doubt, inward division, or another state? The supplied German is corrupt (etwas 00an Gott. zweifelte); verify before adding an idiom or sense.
Collate 25/65: entry has ʕal-am=miṯe, supplied verse has ʕam am miṯe. No automatic text correction is justified without the edition.
Confirm segmentation of Flaġe, kfolaġnən, fliġəlle and fliġənne; retain exact spelling. PrS 82/25 has singular-looking Fləġle against a plural German subject.
Should the p/f spelling entries plġ and flġ be cross-referenced or consolidated? Keep old prs page/line references distinct from supplied text/verse numbers until concordance is checked.
Division/distribution applies to troops, marriage partners, food, merchandise and inheritances, as well as money; participant changes do not establish separate meanings.
Detransitive includes general divisibility, reflexive formation of groups and resultant factional division.
External recipients may be l-marked, besides reciprocal ʕal ruḥayye / ʕal ḥḏoḏe.
